chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'From the respect of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is respecting the aged old man.'

key_terms.إِجْلَال: Respect, veneration, or honoring with deep reverence
key_terms.الشَّيْخِ الْكَبِيرِ: The aged old man, referring to an elderly person deserving of honor
key_terms.عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ: Mighty and Majestic, an honorific title for Allah

ai.seo_question: What is the religious significance of respecting the elderly in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links the veneration of the elderly directly to the magnification of Allah’s glory, establishing it as a tangible act of worship (*ibadah*) rather than mere social courtesy. This concept is deeply rooted in Shia jurisprudence, where respect for the aged is often categorized under *Ihtram al-Muslim* (honoring the believer), reflecting the divine attributes of wisdom and experience manifested in human form. The narration underscores that neglecting the elderly is akin to diminishing the honor of the Creator, thereby elevating a social virtue to a theological imperative.
